title: Kernel fidelity vs throughput exploratory scan — Jul 2027
content:
Purpose and context:
This note captures an exploratory scan comparing kernel-level implementations across quantization regimes with an explicit focus on fidelity (model output perturbation) vs raw throughput (tokens/s) and latency tail behavior. Goal is to surface when kernel choices create non-linear fidelity regressions (not just small metric deltas) while giving substantial throughput wins, and identify safe heuristics for automatic routing in the runtime.

High-level takeaways (TL;DR):
- Some micro-optimizing kernels (lane-tiling + fused-softmax) give 1.4–1.8x throughput on short sequences (<=64) under INT8/AWQ, but introduce brittle activations for a subset of prompt shapes (few-shot prompts, long KV reuse).
- FP8 kernels consistently improve throughput over FP32 but show smaller fidelity variance vs INT8; INT8 GPTQ variants produce the largest divergence for out-of-distribution prompts.
- Memory-bound kernels reduce p95 latency jitter across multi-tenant hosts; compute-bound kernels push p99 up during garbage/GC-like spikes in host scheduling.
- Practical heuristic: prefer FP8 kernels for mixed-criticality routes; reserve “aggressive INT8 kernel” for routes with eval-guard rails and small context windows.

Experimental setup (quick):
- Hardware: 8x A100S (40GB) nodes, isolated single-model per-GPU runs, CUDA 12.3, cuBLASLt where applicable.
- Models: Llama2-13B-chat (base -> quant variants produced by our GPTQ and AWQ pipeline), small reference model opt-2.7B for fast iteration.
- Quantizations tested: INT8 (per-channel, GPTQ), INT8-AWQ (block-wise), FP8 (E4M3-like config), FP16 baseline, FP32 baseline.
- Kernels: matmul-std, matmul-tiling-vec4, fused-attn-softmax, kv-cache-compact, matmul-tiling-vector-lane (vendor-accelerated), custom-reduce-gemm.
- Workloads: (A) short single-turn prompts (avg 30 tokens) synthetic uniform; (B) few-shot instruction prompts (avg 120 tokens); (C) long-context chat (cached KV warm); (D) adversarial test set (counterfactual/paraphrase heavy).
- Metrics captured: tokens/s (steady-state), p50/p95/p99 latency, perplexity delta (on held-out eval set), embedding cosine drift, end-to-end output regression score (ROUGE/EM-like), and qualitative flags (broken numerics, token duplication).
- Harness: deterministic repeat runs (seeded), 20 warm-up sequences then 500 measured sequences per cell.

Selected detailed findings:
1) Short-context throughput wins vs fidelity cliffs:
- Kernel: matmul-tiling-vector-lane + fused-attn-softmax
- Config: INT8-AWQ block size 32, activation calibration from 512 samples
- Result: tokens/s +78% vs FP16 baseline at seq=32, p50 latency -40ms.
- Fidelity: average perplexity delta +1.4% (OK), but on adversarial set we observed a 6.2% perplexity jump and repeated token sequences in 3/500 runs. Error patterns suggest quantized softmax underflow in tails for certain attention score distributions.
- Notes: these failures correlate strongly with near-zero attention scores on long-key contexts where kv-cache rewrite happened.

2) FP8 as a middle-ground:
- Kernel: matmul-std with FP8 E4M3 equiv path + fused-attn-softmax (FP8-accel)
- Result: tokens/s +28% vs FP16, perplexity delta +0.6% median, adversarial delta +1.2%.
- Latency tails: significantly more stable than INT8 kernels (p99 reduced by ~18% vs INT8 variants).
- Operational implication: FP8 offers predictable wins with low fidelity risk; good candidate for default "safe-speed" routes.

3) GPTQ (per-channel) with compute-optimized kernels:
- Kernel: custom-reduce-gemm + kv-cache-compact, GPTQ per-channel 6-bit-like packing
- Result: throughput +35% vs FP16, but we measured outlier fidelity regressions in specific model layers (notably layer 9–11 in Llama2-13B where scale factors are high).
- Observed failure mode: rare numeric saturation causing improbable token selections on numeric or factual prompts.

4) Memory-bound kernels and multi-tenant behavior:
- Kernel: kv-cache-compact + matmul-std
- Behavior: Lower memory footprint reduces cross-process eviction and page thrash, leading to p95 latency reductions in noisy co-located envs. For quantized models this matters: an INT8 kernel that is compute-heavy but memory-sparse can still lose to a memory-friendly FP8 kernel in multi-tenant setups.

5) Sequence-length sensitivity surface:
- Short seq (<=64): tiling/lane kernels dominate; INT8 variants shine.
- Medium seq (64–512): advantage shifts to FP8 and memory-friendly kernels; INT8 gains drop due to increased KV traffic and activation accumulation error.
- Long seq (>512): FP16/FP32 baselines are still safest; quantization errors accumulate in long KV chains.

Qualitative failure examples (anonymized prompts):
- Few-shot arithmetic prompt: INT8-AWQ kernel output repeated a subtraction line twice and returned a wrong final numeric token; FP8/FP16 correct.
- Context-mixing prompt with paraphrase: INT8-GPTQ variant produced hallucinated facts (very low probability but reproducible after warm-up).

Microbench recommendations for runtime heuristics:
1) Route by route metadata: store canonical eval prompt-set per route (short synthetic + representative long-contexts). Run lightweight fidelity probe on first 1000 tokens of traffic to classify safe kernels.
2) Sequence-aware kernel selection: if median observed sequence length > 128, prefer FP8 or FP16 kernels; if <= 64 favor INT8/AWQ kernels but continue monitoring fidelity.
3) Kernel health checks: continuously track embedding cosine drift and a small set of ROUGE-like checks to detect live regressions; auto-fallback to safer kernel if drift threshold exceeded (suggested drift threshold 0.015 cosine).
4) Warm-start validation: after model rollouts, run a 1k-sequence synthetic sweep with both default and aggressive kernels to have a safety delta recorded before switching traffic.

Proposed additions to benchmark harness (actionable):
- Add attention score distribution sampler to detect softmax underflow-prone patterns. This can run in ~10ms per sequence and tag sequences for special handling.
- Implement a low-cost checksum of the KV cache after warm-up to detect packing/saturation anomalies in quantized kernels.
- Extend adversarial prompt corpus with targeted numeric/citation prompts and a small set of few-shot arithmetic/parsing tests.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Can we engineer a cheap per-request scalar that predicts quantization fragility? (e.g., attention sparsity + top-k score variance). If yes, it would enable per-request fallback without global route policy changes.
- How much of the INT8 fidelity cliff is due to our AWQ packing alignment vs kernel floating implementation? Need cross-compare vendor kernels vs our custom kernels at identical bit-packing.
- Are there model-layer-specific quantization strategies that would avoid layer 9–11 saturation observed in Llama2-13B? (per-layer mixed precision suggested).

Immediate next steps (2 week scope):
- Run cross-kernel deterministic comparison on opt-2.7B across full adversarial suite (owner: Marcus).
- Implement attention-distribution sampler in the harness and run on 10k anonymized production-like traces (owner: Priya).
- Draft a playbook for route-level kernel gating and lifecycle (owner: Avery).

Appendix: raw numbers (representative cell, median of 3 runs):
- FP16 baseline (seq32): tokens/s 4100, p95 85ms, perplexity delta 0.0%
- FP8-kernel (seq32): tokens/s 5250, p95 73ms, perplexity delta +0.6%
- INT8-AWQ-tiling (seq32): tokens/s 7300, p95 49ms, perplexity delta +1.4% (adversarial +6.2%)
- GPTQ-perchannel (seq32): tokens/s 5550, p95 78ms, perplexity delta +1.1%
- FP8-kernel (seq256): tokens/s 1100, p95 220ms, perplexity delta +0.9%
- INT8-AWQ-tiling (seq256): tokens/s 1200, p95 380ms, perplexity delta +3.9%

Notes on reproducibility: harness and config saved in linked PR; runs used commit sha: d4f9a6a2, container image: redwood/serving-bench:2027-07-01. All raw traces and activation dumps archived in internal S3 used by the bench team.

Questions for design review meeting:
- Is conservative FP8-first routing acceptable as default for hosted tier? Cost delta vs INT8: ~12–20% tokens cost increase but lower support noise.
- Should Dedicated customers be given an "aggressive" kernel toggle with explicit fidelity acceptance checkbox? (legal/CS implication).

End of note.
